Follow the canonical procedure in `.cadence/reference/explain-plain.md` exactly.

Read the real source first — never guess or recall from memory.

In written mode (the default), lead with a 1-3 line plain-word takeaway, then bullet anything with more than one part. In tutor mode, one idea per turn, then stop for the reader.

No jargon, metaphors, nested clauses, or raw field names — replace them with what they mean. Tutor mode allows one analogy per idea, with where it stops matching.

If the source doesn't state something, say "not stated," never guess.

Keep every fact from the source; the length rules govern phrasing only — never drop a stated fact to hit them, add another line instead.
